sentences.text: The genus Gobivenator contains only one known species, Gobivenator mongoliensis, which is represented by a single individual.
This small theropod measured approximately 1.7 meters in length and weighed about 9 kilograms.
Like other troodontids, it possessed sickle-claws and raptorial hands, and it had some of the highest non-avian encephalization quotients, indicating advanced behavior and keen senses.
Although the skull was akinetic, it possessed preconditions for the later evolution of cranial kinesis in birds, such as the loss of the epipterygoid bone.
The genus was first described and named by Tsuihiji et al. in 2014, with the name derived from the Gobi Desert and the Latin word venator, meaning hunter.
A Japanese-Mongolian expedition discovered the holotype at the Dzamin Khond locality in the Djadokhta Formation.
The specimen dates to approximately 72 million years ago during the late Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
Its keen senses and advanced behavior likely aided in hunting.
The high non-avian encephalization quotients suggest the animal was behaviorally advanced.
A 2024 study recovered Gobivenator as a basal member of the Troodontinae, as the sister taxon to Hypnovenator.
It is classified as a Saurischian theropod dinosaur in the family Troodontidae and subfamily Troodontinae.
Gobivenator lived during the late Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in the central Gobi Desert, Mongolia.
